**Continuous 2.18.0**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.16.3, 2.16.2, 2.16.1, 2.16.0, 2.14.0, 2.12.x, 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.18.0.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.18.0.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.18.0.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.18.0.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.18.0.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.18.0.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.18.0.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.18.0-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.18.0.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.18.0-vscode/continuous-cli-2.18.0.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). The short command `cn` also works; both run the same program. It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.16.3

Model information now comes from the providers themselves. Test connection checks that the model id you configured exists, the selected Anthropic or OpenAI model's context window and retirement date are refreshed from its own API, and Bedrock warns about a 0 quota before the first request and prices from the AWS Price List. Every cost now says where its prices came from and as of when, and a model nothing else prices can fall back to the community catalogue at models.dev. Under the prompt, a context meter shows what fills the context window. Each policy control gains **Custom…**, which opens an editor for your levels, rule lists and `permissions.yaml` settings. Models get a **Configure** dialog, and the agents panel is grouped into Active, Done and Archived.

Three new hosts can be contacted, and the selected model's own API is asked about that model in the background. All of this follows **Model information updates**: **Off** stops all of it. The details are under Behaviour changes.

### Behaviour changes

- **New egress: `models.dev`, a last-resort price from the community catalogue.** When a selected model has no price from a price you entered, a provider list (OpenRouter's, or the AWS Price List for Bedrock) or the built-in tables, Continuous can price it from [models.dev](https://models.dev) (community-maintained, MIT). Such figures are labelled "community catalogue (models.dev), &lt;date&gt; — estimate". The catalogue never replaces a better source. `--max-budget-usd` is refused on a community-only price unless you pass `--budget-allow-unpriced`, which holds the cap on the estimate. The Auto reviewer's shadow budget is never held on it.
  - **What is sent**: one `GET https://models.dev/api.json` (TCP 443). It carries no key, body or model name, and only the headers `accept: application/json` and `user-agent: continuous`. The whole catalogue is downloaded, so models.dev does not learn which model you use.
  - **When**: only while a selected model (the IDE's chat or reviewer model, or the terminal agent's model) has no better price, and never when model information updates are **Off**. Under **Automatic** (the default), the first check comes 15 to 60 seconds after the IDE starts or 1 to 3 seconds after the terminal agent starts, then at least every 6 hours. A download happens only when the local copy is missing or older than the refresh interval (24 hours). Failures back off from 5 minutes up to 6 hours. Under **Only when I ask**, it happens only on **Refresh now** in the IDE. `cn serve` does not fetch it. On a fresh profile with an unpriced model selected (a Mistral, Gemini or Groq model, for example), expect one request per start-up. With only Anthropic, OpenAI, Bedrock or OpenRouter models selected, expect none.
  - **Kept**: prices only, at most 4 MB, in `model-catalog/models-dev.json`.
- **New egress, Bedrock only: `pricing.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` (the AWS Price List).** Cost estimates for Bedrock models use the public AWS Price List for the selected model's region, ahead of the built-in prices, and name it with its date. Flex and priority requests are priced at their own rates where AWS lists them.
  - **What is sent**: one `GET https://pricing.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/offers/v1.0/aws/AmazonBedrock/current/<region>/index.json` (TCP 443). It carries no AWS credentials or account id, only the headers `accept` and `user-agent: continuous`. The file is large; it is streamed, with at most 256 MB downloaded and 120 seconds allowed.
  - **When**: only when a Bedrock model is configured, and only for the selected model's region. Under **Automatic**, it is fetched when you select a Bedrock model, on Bedrock Test connection, and in the background once per refresh interval. Under **Only when I ask**, only on Bedrock Test connection. Under **Off**, never.
  - **Kept**: per-token prices and their date, in `model-catalog/bedrock-prices-<region>.json`.
- **New egress, Bedrock only: `servicequotas.<region>.amazonaws.com` (an optional quota check).** `ListServiceQuotas` for service code `bedrock` is signed with the same AWS credentials as your Bedrock requests. It only reads your account's applied quotas and changes nothing. It runs with the same timing as the Price List, takes at most 5 seconds and makes one attempt. A Bedrock API key cannot sign it, so the check is skipped for keys.
  - **Kept**: quota names and values, or the fact that the permission is missing, in `model-catalog/bedrock-quotas-<hash>.json`. No key, secret or account id is stored.
- **The selected Anthropic or OpenAI chat model's details are refreshed from its own provider.** Under **Automatic**, Continuous sends one `GET {apiBase}/models/{id}` with your key and `requestOptions` 3 to 5 seconds after you select the model, then once per refresh interval (24 hours by default). It asks only the API base configured for that model, so no new host is contacted. Nothing waits for the answer, and the lookup times out after 5 seconds. Failures back off from 5 minutes up to 6 hours, never sooner than `retry-after`. An endpoint without a models API is not asked again in that session.
  - **What it changes**: the answer supplies the context window and default maximum output where your config does not set them, ahead of the bundled model data. Anthropic's built-in default of 8192 output tokens is never raised by it.
  - **Retirement dates**: a deprecation, retirement or shutdown date shows as the warning chip beside the model picker, now for OpenAI models too.
  - **Kept**: the answer, in `model-catalog/provider-<provider>-<hash>.json`. The key is not written.
  - **Other settings**: **Only when I ask** limits the lookup to Test connection. **Off** sends nothing and ignores kept answers. The terminal agent does not run this refresh.
- **The context meter replaces the battery.** The small battery that appeared from 60 percent, with Compact and New session in a hover tooltip, is gone. Those actions are now in the context meter's panel (see New).

### New

- **Test connection checks the model id.** For Anthropic, OpenAI and OpenAI-compatible servers that have a models list, Test connection asks the provider about the configured id with `GET /v1/models/{id}`. This applies in the add-model form and in `continuous test-connection --model`.
  - **Unknown ids**: an id the key cannot reach is named, with close matches from the list ("Did you mean claude-opus-5-5?").
  - **Details**: Anthropic's answer adds the context window, maximum output, image and PDF input, thinking types and deprecation dates. OpenAI's adds a shutdown date.
  - **Problems are not failures**: a refused key, a rate limit, a network failure and an endpoint without a models API are each reported as "not checked". None of them fails the connection or a chat request.
- **Costs say where their prices came from and as of when.** The console's Total Usage, the terminal agent's `/info` and its `--verbose` end-of-run summary add a line such as "Prices: Anthropic list prices, as of 2026-11-02", "Prices: OpenRouter model list, fetched 3 h ago" or "Prices: AWS Price List, us-east-1 in-region, downloaded …".
  - **Served tier**: when Bedrock or Anthropic report that a request was served at a non-standard tier (flex, priority, batch) and it was priced at standard rates, a note says whether the actual charge is lower or higher.
  - **stream-json**: `-p --format stream-json` adds `priceSource` and `servedTier` to each `usage` line, and `priceSources` and `servedTiers` to the `result` line. These fields are optional, so the schema version stays 1.
- **Bedrock names a 0 quota before the first request.** If your AWS credentials may read Service Quotas (`servicequotas:ListServiceQuotas`, optional), Test connection and selecting a Bedrock model warn when the account's tokens-per-minute or requests-per-minute quota for that model is 0 in the region. The warning links to the Service Quotas console. Without the permission, Test connection still succeeds and shows one quiet line, "Quota check skipped: this profile lacks servicequotas:ListServiceQuotas". That answer is remembered per profile and region for a day, or until the credentials change.
- **See what fills the context window.** Beside the session cost under the prompt, a context meter shows the share of the model's window in use ("Context 43%"). It turns the theme's warning colour from 60 percent, and its error colour from 80 percent or once the oldest messages are being left out.
  - **Opening it**: click it, press Enter on it, or rest the pointer on it.
  - **What it shows**: a bar and a table of the system prompt, tool definitions, rules, attached files, your messages, replies, tool calls, tool results, terminal output, images, reasoning, free space and the room kept for the reply. It also names the largest items and shows the prompt cache state. The split is estimated and scaled to the provider's token count.
  - **Actions**: **Compact now** and **New session**. Nothing about what is sent to the model changes.
- **Custom… on every policy control.** The preset picker and each area's control end with **Custom…**, which opens a Custom policy editor on the Permissions page, started from the preset you are on. It covers:
  - the five levels, the built-in rules, and the plan and question settings;
  - your Never, Ask, Always and Always-on Never lists: add, remove or move rules, with a live preview against your recent calls;
  - the MCP servers you trust and the MCP tools Plan mode may use;
  - a review of every change before it is saved.

  `floor:`, `mcpServers`, `plan.mcpTools`, `plan.allowTerminal` and `questions.delivery` in `permissions.yaml` can now be changed from the extension. The file's comments are kept. Workspace, assistant and terminal-agent rules are never copied into your lists.

- **Configure… dialog for a model.** The gear on a model, in the chat model picker and on each row of the Models settings page, opens **Configure &lt;model&gt;**. It is a dialog to view, change and check the settings `config.yaml` already has for that model, on four tabs: Connection (with Test connection), Capabilities, Generation, and Context & cost.
  - **Previews**: **Review changes** shows the YAML diff before it is saved. Comments, key order and keys the dialog does not manage are kept.
  - **Keys**: a typed API key goes to secure storage or `.env`, never into `config.yaml`.
  - **Prices**: the Context & cost tab shows the price budgets use and where it comes from.
- **Agents panel grouped Active, Done and Archived.** The agents panel above the chat input lists running and waiting agents first. Finished agents collapse into one Done line, with **Archive all**. Opening a row shows that agent's record, read-only, with Stop, Archive or Restore, and Show in conversation. **Back to Session** or Escape returns to the list. Archiving only hides an agent in the panel: the session and its history are unchanged.

### Fixes

- **Bedrock errors name the cause when a model is refused for quota or account reasons.**
  - "Not available for this account" is what Bedrock answers when the account's tokens-per-minute quota for the model is 0, even with model access granted. It now points at Service Quotas instead of the model access page.
  - "Your account is currently being verified" (the first use of a region) now says to wait.
  - A throttled request says the quota is used up, and that throttling on the very first request can mean a quota of 0.
- **A Bedrock model configured with `serviceTier: flex` or `priority` is no longer priced silently at standard rates.** The cost says which tier served the request. With the AWS Price List it is priced at that tier's own rates.
- **Model lists keep more of what providers report.** Adding Anthropic models reads image support and the scheduled retirement date from Anthropic's model list. The Bedrock model list keeps image support and the legacy, extended-access and end-of-life dates Bedrock reports.

- **README, Marketplace README and install guide updated to the current releases.** The guide documents the `-agents.vsix` build. The `gh`, PowerShell and macOS install commands now match only the normal build, where they used to download both. The social banner uses the current mark. Old-logo and upstream assets are removed, and 29 docs redirects that pointed at moved pages are fixed.
- **The docs site builds again.** Its deploy had failed since 2026-11-11 on pages MDX could not compile.
- **Bedrock**: the Bedrock page has an "Optional quota check" section with the IAM policy snippet, and a section on prices from the AWS Price List. `PRIVACY.md` and the egress allowlist list each new host.
- **Research notes** in `plans/research/`, design only:
  - custom policy and IDGAF-plus-guards concept review;
  - subagent sessions phase 2 (retained transcripts, messages, resume);
  - taint by provenance;
  - an OS sandbox for agent terminal commands;
  - an audit of message validity across providers;
  - session forking and selective compaction against the prompt cache;
  - provider model metadata;
  - the context usage breakdown;
  - the model configuration dialog;
  - the Custom policy editor;
  - the agents panel;
  - next improvements nobody has asked for yet.

### Upgrade notes

- **Firewalls and sandboxes.** Expect `models.dev` while an unpriced model is selected. Machines with a Bedrock model configured can contact `pricing.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` and `servicequotas.<region>.amazonaws.com`. All on TCP 443.
- **Stopping the new requests.** Set **Model information updates** to **Off** to stop every request above. Use `continuous.modelInformationUpdates` in VS Code, the Models settings page, `modelCatalog: off` in `~/.continuous/config.yaml`, or `CONTINUOUS_MODEL_INFO_UPDATES=off`. **Only when I ask** limits them to explicit actions: Test connection and Refresh now.
- **Bedrock quota check.** The check needs `servicequotas:ListServiceQuotas`. It is optional: without it, nothing fails and nothing is retried for a day.
- **Budgets on community prices.** `--max-budget-usd` on a model whose only price is from models.dev is refused at start-up. Pass `--budget-allow-unpriced` to hold the cap on the estimate.
- **Always-on Never at IDGAF.** The Custom policy editor writes `floor:` rules. As in 2.16.3, they bind at every level below IDGAF; at IDGAF the call runs and the audit trail records the rule.
